title: How to Survive a Tiger Attack

lines.text: A Bengal tiger attacks from behind at forty miles per hour.
lines.say: A Bengal tiger attacks from behind at forty miles per hour.
lines.caps: A Bengal tiger *attacks | from *behind | at *forty miles per hour.

lines.text: Rule one: never run, because fleeing instantly triggers its deadly chase instinct.
lines.say: Rule one: never run, because fleeing instantly triggers its deadly chase instinct.
lines.caps: *Rule one: | *never run, | because fleeing *instantly triggers | its *deadly chase instinct.

lines.text: Stand tall, lock intense eye contact, and spread your jacket wide overhead.
lines.say: Stand tall, lock intense eye contact, and spread your jacket wide overhead.
lines.caps: *Stand tall, | lock *intense eye contact, | and *spread | your jacket wide *overhead.

lines.text: Back away slowly while shouting loudly or clanging metal to scare it.
lines.say: Back away slowly while shouting loudly or clanging metal to scare it.
lines.caps: Back away *slowly | while *shouting loudly | or *clanging metal | to *scare it.

lines.text: In India's Sundarbans, villagers wear backward face masks to fool ambush predators.
lines.say: In India's Sundarbans, villagers wear backward face masks to fool ambush predators.
lines.caps: In India's *Sundarbans, | *villagers wear backward face masks | to fool ambush *predators.

lines.text: If it lunges, strike the sensitive eyes, nose, and ears with force.
lines.say: If it lunges, strike the sensitive eyes, nose, and ears with force.
lines.caps: If it *lunges, | strike the *sensitive eyes, | *nose, | and ears with *force.

lines.text: Never turn your back—standing your ground saves your life.
lines.say: Never turn your back. Standing your ground saves your life.
lines.caps: *Never turn your back— | standing your *ground saves your life.
